title: Opatija Prices 2027: Realistic Daily Budget Guide
metaDescription: Opatija prices are rising about 4-6% a year. See 2027 budgets for hotels, food, coffee, tourist tax and transport, with real euro figures and money-saving tips.
content:
## How Much Does Opatija Cost in 2027?

Opatija is one of the more expensive towns on the Croatian coast, and its prices sit above the national average. Croatian consumer prices for restaurants and accommodation were 6.1% higher in August 2026 than a year earlier, while overall inflation was 4.2%. Menus and room rates are rising faster than the general consumer basket. Prices for 2027 are not yet published, so the figures below use 2026 prices plus an assumed 4-6% rise.

### 2027 daily budget per person (estimate)

| Travel style | 2026 level | Planning figure for 2027 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Budget | €80-120 | €85-125 |
| Mid-range | €150-300 | €155-310 |
| Luxury | €400+ | €420+ |

These are per-person figures that assume two people sharing a room. Solo travellers should add 30-60% because single occupancy is rarely discounted. Most visitors in a 3-4 star hotel or good apartment, eating one restaurant meal a day, land around €150-220.

## How Have Prices in Opatija Changed Recently?

Three trends matter for planning:

- **Restaurants and hotels are rising faster than shops.** The 6.1% annual increase in restaurants and accommodation, against 4.2% overall inflation, is the clearest signal.
- **Opatija carries a premium inside Croatia.** Café prices illustrate it: a milk coffee in an Opatija hotel café has been reported at up to €6, while a comparable 5-star hotel in Zagreb charges about €3.50.
- **Croatia is no longer a bargain relative to its neighbours.** Croatian restaurants and hotels price at about 95% of the EU average, even though everyday consumer prices overall are at about 73%.

The euro changeover in 2023 removed currency-exchange costs but did not slow price growth. Opatija's prices follow its position as a historic spa resort with many 4- and 5-star hotels, not the wider Kvarner region.

## Accommodation Prices in Opatija

Accommodation is the largest budget item and the one most affected by season.

### Budget: €40-100 per night
Small guesthouses, rooms and apartments away from the seafront cost roughly €40-90, and simple 2-star hotels such as Hotel Gardenija run about €60-100. Apartments in the streets above Maršala Tita, the main road, are cheaper than those along the coast. Expect the 2027 equivalent to be about €45-105.

### Mid-range: €90-250 per night
Three- and four-star hotels on or near Maršala Tita, including the Liburnia group's Hotel Istra, Hotel Kristal and Hotel Lungomare, fall here. Shoulder-season rates at the low end are common in April, May and October. Hotel Istra typically lists at €120-280 and sits 10m from the water.

### Upscale: €150-600 per night
Boutique and historic properties charge €150-350. Hotel Kvarner, Hotel Ambasador and Amadria Park Hotel Milenij sit in the €250-600 band, with the top of the range in July and August. The Imperial, Savoy and Admiral are other established names along the promenade.

### Seasonality
Summer rates (June-August) can run 40-100% above shoulder-season rates. Opatija is also a congress and spa town, so autumn and winter are busier than at purely beach-driven destinations, and hotels stay open all year. Weekends in December and around Easter can be pricey.

### Tourist tax
The tourist tax in Opatija is €2.20 per person per night from 1 April to 30 September and €1.50 for the rest of the year. Children under 12 are exempt and ages 12 to 18 pay half. Hotels usually show it as a separate invoice line, and booking platforms often leave it out of the headline price. For two adults over five summer nights, that is €22.

## Food and Drink Prices

### Cafés and quick bites
- Espresso: €2.00-3.50
- Cappuccino: €2.50-4.00
- Soft drink: €3.00-4.50
- Bakery snack or fast food: €7-12
- Pastry and coffee at a bakery: €2.50-5

The historic cafés on Maršala Tita, such as Caffe Wagner, charge €3-6 per drink. That pays for the setting rather than the coffee. Skip the promenade-front terraces for a daily coffee habit and use a bakery or a side-street café instead; the saving across a week is more than €20 per person.

### Restaurants
- Main course in a mid-range restaurant or konoba: €15-30
- Full meal with starter, main and a glass of wine or beer: €30-50 per person
- Lunch at a traditional restaurant such as Ružmarin: roughly €20-40 per person
- Fine dining, excluding drinks: €60-120 per person
- Fresh fish by the kilo: typically €70-80/kg, so a whole grilled fish for two can reach €50-80

For 2027, add about 5% to each of these. A three-course dinner for two at a mid-range restaurant has been averaging about €60 nationally, and Opatija usually costs more than that.

### Drinks and nightlife
A half-litre of draught beer costs €3.50-5.50 and a glass of local wine €4-7. Cocktails at hotel lounges and upscale bars run €8-15.

### Groceries
Supermarkets such as those in the town centre and in Matulji or Rijeka are far cheaper than eating out. Self-catering breakfast and lunch can cut food spending to €18-28 per person per day.

## Getting Around: Transport Costs

Opatija is compact. The Lungomare coastal promenade stretches about 12km from Volosko to Lovran and is free to walk. Most sights in the centre are within 1-2km of each other.

- **Local bus (single ticket):** about €1.50-2.00 on the local routes. The coastal line connecting Rijeka, Opatija and Lovran is the most useful and runs frequently through the day.
- **Taxi:** short rides inside town are expensive by Croatian standards; for anything over a few kilometres, the bus is the better choice.
- **Car:** parking in the centre is limited and charged by zone, and hotels often add a daily parking fee. For a stay centred on the coast, a car is usually not worth the extra cost.
- **Airports:** Rijeka airport on the island of Krk is the closest, and Pula and Trieste are further options. Rijeka and Pula each make sense for flights with transfers by bus or shuttle.

## Sample 2027 Budgets

### Budget: about €85-125 per person per day
Guesthouse or apartment room share (€30-50 each), bakery breakfast, groceries for lunch, one casual dinner (€12-20), free beach and Lungomare time. Use a public beach platform instead of a hotel pool.

### Mid-range: about €155-250 per person per day
Three- or four-star hotel (€80-130 per person), café breakfast or hotel buffet, a konoba dinner at €30-50, a couple of coffees and a drink, local buses.

### Luxury: €420+ per person per day
Five-star room (€150-300 each), fine dining at €70-120, spa treatments and private transfers.

### Weekend example (two people, two nights, shoulder season)
Hotel at €150/night = €300, tourist tax €6 off-season, meals €160, coffees and drinks €40, local transport €10. Total roughly €515 for two, or about €255 each.

## Money-Saving Tips for Opatija in 2027

1. **Travel in May, June, late September or October.** Sea temperatures are suitable for swimming through September, and room rates drop noticeably against July and August.
2. **Stay slightly uphill or in neighbouring Ičići, Volosko or Lovran.** The Lungomare connects them, and rooms there cost less than on Maršala Tita.
3. **Book half-board only if the restaurant is good.** In many Opatija hotels, a standalone dinner in town costs less than the half-board supplement, so this is usually not worth the extra cost.
4. **Eat the main meal at lunch.** Many restaurants offer cheaper daily set menus at midday.
5. **Check the invoice for tourist tax and parking.** Both are routinely excluded from comparison-site prices.
6. **Walk the Lungomare instead of paying for tours.** The promenade, the Maiden with the Seagull statue and Park Angiolina are free.
7. **Day-trip to Rijeka** for cheaper groceries and restaurant meals, then return by the coastal bus.

## Is Opatija Worth the Price?

Opatija costs more than Rijeka, Lovran or Istrian inland towns, and noticeably more than most of continental Croatia. The premium buys Belle Époque architecture, parks, an all-year season and a flat, walkable coast. For a short stay, it holds up well. For a long beach holiday on a tight budget, an apartment in Lovran or Medveja gives better value.

faq.question: How much does a day in Opatija cost in 2027?
faq.answer: A realistic budget is €85-125 per person for budget travel, €155-250 for mid-range, and €420+ for luxury. These figures are 2026 prices plus an assumed 4-6% increase. Costs are highest in July and August.

faq.question: Is Opatija expensive compared with the rest of Croatia?
faq.answer: Yes. Opatija is among the pricier coastal towns, mainly because of its many 4- and 5-star hotels and its upmarket cafés. Coffee in hotel cafés has been reported at up to €6, versus about €2-3 in ordinary cafés elsewhere in Croatia.

faq.question: How much is the tourist tax in Opatija?
faq.answer: The tax is €2.20 per person per night between 1 April and 30 September, and €1.50 for the rest of the year. Children under 12 are exempt and ages 12 to 18 pay half. It is often shown as a separate line on the hotel invoice.

faq.question: How much does a meal cost in Opatija?
faq.answer: A main course in a konoba or mid-range restaurant costs €15-30, and a full meal with a drink is usually €30-50 per person. A bakery or fast-food meal costs €7-12, and fine dining starts around €60 per person.

faq.question: What is the cheapest time to visit Opatija?
faq.answer: Late autumn, winter (outside December weekends) and early spring have the lowest room rates. For swimming weather at lower prices, May, June and late September to early October are the best compromise.

faq.question: How much does a hotel in Opatija cost per night?
faq.answer: Budget guesthouses cost about €40-100, 3-4 star hotels €90-250, and 5-star or luxury hotels €250-600 per night. Add roughly 5% for 2027 and check whether tourist tax and parking are included.

faq.question: Do I need a car in Opatija?
faq.answer: Usually not. The centre is walkable, the Lungomare connects the neighbouring towns, and a local bus links Opatija with Rijeka and Lovran for roughly €1.50-2.00 per ride. Parking in town is limited and costs extra.

quickAnswer: Plan on €80-120 per person per day on a tight budget, €150-250 mid-range, and €400+ for luxury in Opatija in 2027. Restaurant and accommodation prices in Croatia rose 6.1% year on year in August 2026, so a further 4-6% increase is a sensible planning assumption for 2027.
